name: Lethderg

attributes.attribute: the daughter of the great king of Ulster
carried off by the war band of Fothad
bears the compound name Medb Lethderg

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lethderg is an Irish heroine or goddess. Her name occurs in the Dindshenchas, the old Irish verses that map out the names of places. There she is the daughter of the great king of Ulster, Concobar mac Nessa. A war band under a minor king, Fothad, carried her off. The faint story marks a kind of sovereignty goddess. That goddess sets a king on the throne when she gives herself to him. The title also joins the name of the great queen Medb.

okr.objective: Hold the sovereignty goddess Lethderg in a compact sourced entry.
key_results: Name her father Concobar and her captor Fothad.
Link her name to Medb and the kingship goddess.
